title: VISUAL SCHEMA — MOVING STATUES MADE OF RUBIES MIND (MSMRM) Material Symbol Aesthetic / Room-Integrity Hand Diagram
creator: Lee Sharks
description: This render specification maps MSMRM as a manual semantic apparatus: a room, a five-document hand, and an integrity lock. Its image is meant to be used as a room map rather than viewed as decorative illustration. The Material Symbol aesthetic makes provenance, document function, reconstruction, and the holographic relation among parts visually load-bearing.
reading: Force -> Closure -> Growth -> Text -> Method -> Closure
wiki_article: The *Visual Schema for Moving Statues Made of Rubies Mind* is a render specification for a five-part memographic room. It organizes the room as a hand whose palm and wrist hold the charter and integrity lock while five upward articulations hold the document functions. Faceted ruby masses represent concentrated and cut semantic value; the room frame prevents the hand from becoming an isolated emblem; citation glyphs, reconstruction arrows, and containment-vessel outlines show how the documents refer to one another and how the whole may be rebuilt from a surviving part. The schema uses the Material Symbol aesthetic: sacred-technical, tactile, diagrammatic, and operational. Every visual element must carry a governance function. The hand is therefore not a metaphor pasted over the archive family. It is the room’s navigation and integrity structure. Its five holdings correspond to the provenance anchor, experimental pointer, transformation demonstration, disciplinary binding, and seal. The holographic principle “each part contains the whole” governs the rendering. A document should preserve enough cross-reference and structural information to reconstruct the hand; removal of those relations produces holographic collapse. Broken or bypassed vessels represent the room’s refusal of both supernatural closure and dismissive closure. This schema should be linked directly to the MSMRM charter at record #505 and to the five memographic holdings that follow. It is the visual-operational surface of that room, not a substitute for its charter.
